problem: Prior single/few-image indoor view synthesis under large viewpoint changes (Pathdreamer, PixelSynth) relies on complex multi-stage pipelines (semantic segmentation inputs, stochastic structure generators, SPADE layers, VQ-VAE/PixelCNN support sets, multi-sample reranking), and no prior view-synthesis model had shown benefits as data augmentation for VLN.
motivation: Simpler models that need no semantic segmentation can be trained on broader RGB-D and video data and can serve embodied AI as world models or augmenters. VLN agents overfit to the incidental details of the fixed captured panorama locations, so synthesizing panoramas at perturbed positions could improve generalization to unseen environments.
key_idea: A single-stage image-to-image GAN (partial-conv ResNet-101 encoder-decoder trained with random masking) maps reprojected point-cloud guidance images directly to high-resolution RGB-D, and its novel-view panoramas are used to spatially perturb VLN training trajectories.
insight: Random masking of up to 75% of guidance pixels plus extra receptive-field conv layers is critical: removing them raises FID@1 from 19.6 to 24.2 and FID@1-6 from 58.0 to 68.0. The VGG perceptual loss and the KLD/noise module each hurt multi-step FID (58.0 to 66.5 and 58.0 to 65.2), and using GT depth in the GAN loss hurts too, so RGB-depth consistency matters. In VLN, view-synthesized perturbations help (+~1% SR), while SimCLR image augmentation, Habitat renders alone and Pathdreamer alone do not, and combining Habitat with the GAN gives the best SR.
method: Guidance images: accumulate RGB-D context (and generated predictions in multi-step rollouts) into a point cloud and reproject to the target pose; equirectangular camera for Matterport3D, perspective for RealEstate10K.

Generator: RedNet-style encoder-decoder with a ResNet-101 encoder using partial convolutions, a shared encoder for RGB and depth, separate transposed-ResNet-101 decoders for RGB and depth, and skip connections.
Receptive field: four extra 3x3 conv layers after the encoder to propagate non-local information for large outpainting.
Losses: hinge GAN loss with a multi-scale PatchGAN discriminator on 4-channel RGB-D, plus L1 depth loss (lambda_GAN=1, lambda_D=100); no VGG perceptual loss, no SVG/KLD stochastic module.
Training: from scratch, single-step prediction only, random masking of up to 75% of guidance pixels; on RE10K, MiDaS depth with COLMAP-based training data.

Trajectory augmentation for VLN: resample each training panorama location uniformly within ±1.5 m horizontally and ±0.1 m vertically (rejecting perturbations through walls), generate the panorama at 1024x512 from the two nearest GT RGB-D panos, and train the VLN-BERT agent (with MURAL features) on it, optionally mixed with Habitat renders.

setting.backbone: ResNet-101 partial-conv encoder-decoder GAN (trained from scratch); VLN agent is Recurrent VLN-BERT with MURAL-large (EfficientNet-B7) image features
setting.training_data: Matterport3D (11K RGB-D panos, 90 buildings) for view synthesis; RealEstate10K (6,865 videos, 67,834 COLMAP-reconstructed sub-sequences, MiDaS depth) for the RE10K model; R2R 14K instruction-trajectory pairs for VLN. MURAL is pretrained on 1.8B web image-text pairs.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (Matterport3D) / monocular RGB with estimated depth (RE10K); VLN agent uses 360° panoramas
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (R2R); Habitat used for mesh-render augmentation baseline
setting.privileged: GT depth and camera poses for context panos in Matterport3D view synthesis and augmentation (train-time only for VLN); none at VLN test time

numbers_note: Main contribution numbers are FID for view synthesis (Matterport3D val-unseen 1-step FID 19.6, 1-6 steps 58.0 with 1 context; RE10K FID 23.5 all / 21.5 indoor), which are not navigation benchmarks and are omitted from the numbers list. Baseline VLN-BERT+MURAL (no perturbation): val-unseen NE 3.58, SR 67.3, SPL 60.9.
results: The GAN cuts Matterport3D val-unseen FID from 27.2 to 19.6 (1 step) and 65.8 to 58.0 (1-6 steps) versus Pathdreamer, and RE10K FID from 25.5 to 23.5 versus PixelSynth; humans prefer it over Pathdreamer 60.4% and over PixelSynth 77.3% of the time. As VLN augmentation it lifts R2R val-unseen SR from 67.3 to 68.1 (68.8 with Habitat), and it reaches 66 SR on the test-unseen set, above HAMT's 65.
limitations: Worse than Pathdreamer on multi-step FID in seen environments, and it is deterministic (no diversity) since the stochastic module was dropped
VLN gains are small (about 1-1.5% SR) and validated only for one agent on R2R, with Val-Seen performance dropping under augmentation
Depends on GT or estimated depth and poses for context, and RE10K experiments need scale alignment of MiDaS depth to the baseline's depth
